open_points.subject: disclosure-class order
open_points.text: “the members and the order have that one home” (`models`), but `canonical_values` also “Owns ... The order of disclosure classes”
open_points.question: Does `models` own the disclosure-class order while `canonical_values` only applies it, or does `canonical_values` own the order itself?
options: `models` owns the enumeration and its order; `canonical_values` provides comparison and highest-class behavior
`canonical_values` owns the disclosure-class order, while `models` only declares the members
open_points.default_guess: Keep the members and order in `models`; make `canonical_values` consume that order when comparing classes.

open_points.subject: randomly minted entity identities
open_points.text: A01 rule 2 requires `trial_execution_id`, `binding_id`, `run_id`, `approval_id` and `grant_id` to be “minted at random by the kernel” and reminted on collision, while `canonical_values` owns only “A01 rules 1 and 4” and no State 3 module is assigned A01 rule 2 or a random-ID capability.
open_points.question: Which module owns random-ID generation, collision checking and reminting, and how do `functions`, `bindings`, `runs` and `effects` obtain those IDs without duplicating that mechanism?
options: `store` atomically mints and collision-checks IDs while creating records
A lower identity utility such as `canonical_values` mints candidates and `store` checks collisions
Each record-owning module independently mints IDs and retries after `store` reports a collision
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check each random entity ID inside the record-creation transaction.
